mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand but expansion in residential investment, which historically precedes a mild, short-lived equity pullback over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST > previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a housing bubble.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered periods, or the effect inverts during a war shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days unless offset by a concurrent rise in consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS).
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes where INDPRO is below threshold and RSAFS does not rise by at least 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which historically precedes equity market volatility but not a directional bias; however, when combined with a concurrent rise in PAYEMS, it predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and PAYEMS rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential rise in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals strengthening demand fundamentals, which drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both rise for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the employment-population ratio above its 10-year average by more than 0.5 percentage points signals a tight labor market, which consistently predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes during a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days unless offset by a simultaneous surge in consumer spending (RSAFS).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-mo MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes where RSAFS does not surge by at least 1.0%.
